clue.text: A French intellectual-almost drunk, regardless

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for drunk is dropped

parts.note: un is the French word for a
a great mind is an intellectual
full is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A French thinker, half-cut, carrying on regardless of everything around him.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unmindful pays no heed, which is acting regardless of consequences or warnings.

clue.text: Disturbed when riding on 19ac

parts.note: a jockey who is up is riding
the answer to 19 across; on places it below in a down clue

explanation.surface: Someone put out while sitting on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To be upset is to be emotionally troubled or agitated, which is being disturbed.

clue.text: Old dance Shakespeare wrote for this?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stately dance of the Elizabethan era

definitions.note: a cryptic hint at the play title Measure for Measure
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Shakespeare wrote a comedy whose title repeats one word around for

explanation.surface: A historic dance that Shakespeare composed a piece for.
explanation.walkthrough: The play is Measure for Measure, so Shakespeare literally wrote the word for after this one.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure was a grave, formal dance, and the play title puts the same word on both sides of for.

clue.text: Bad thing to occur at the end of the day

definitions.text: Bad thing to occur at the end of the day

parts.note: surface reading: some misfortune, like a tumble, that happens late

parts.words: at the end of the day
parts.note: setter's reading: the event that literally comes as daylight finishes, a descent of darkness

explanation.surface: A mishap that strikes in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: A bad thing to occur suggests an accident such as a fall; the fall here is of darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightfall is dusk, the time when darkness descends at the close of daylight hours.

clue.text: Every one in a remote circle having extensive influence

parts.note: far means distant

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the other two

parts.note: a ring is a circle
each means every one

explanation.surface: Everyone in a far-off clique wields wide power.
explanation.definitionFit: Far-reaching effects or powers stretch a long way and affect many people, a wide-ranging sway.

clue.text: Housman's Salopian left a small daughter

parts.note: L is short for left
taken as written
small means abbreviated, and d is short for daughter

explanation.surface: A man from Shropshire in Housman's poems walked out on his little girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Salopian means from Shropshire, an English county; A.E. Housman's best-known poems are A Shropshire Lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Housman's collection is A Shropshire Lad, so his Salopian is a young fellow from that county.

clue.text: Timothy, the copper's nark

definitions.meaning: first meaning: timothy is a meadow plant grown for hay
second meaning: a police informer, in British slang

explanation.surface: Someone called Timothy is unmasked as the informer feeding the police.
explanation.walkthrough: Timothy looks like a man's name but is a fodder plant. A copper is a policeman and a nark is an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Timothy is one species of pasture plant, and an informer who betrays criminals to police is called this in slang.

clue.text: Proceed across American square, displaying zest

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the verb stretches either side of the other pieces

parts.note: to go is to proceed
US is short for American
a T-square is a drawing tool

explanation.surface: Moving across an American town square with energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment and enthusiasm, the same eager relish that zest describes.

clue.text: A couple of states suppressing the church's greed

parts.note: taken as written
VA and RI are the postal codes for Virginia and Rhode Island
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Two US states holding down a church's money-grubbing.
explanation.walkthrough: Suppressing works by position: in a down clue the states sit on top of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an excessive desire for wealth, one of the seven deadly sins also called greed.

clue.text: Severe, but ecstatic about part of Hertfordshire

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for ecstatic surrounds the place

parts.note: sent is slang for transported with delight
Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire, an English county north of London

explanation.surface: Stern, yet thrilled by some corner of Hertfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent rules are strict and demanding, the same rigour that severe conveys.

clue.text: Shock makes us walk unsteadily

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to astonish or amaze someone
second meaning: to totter or lurch along

explanation.surface: A sudden fright leaves us tottering about.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to astonish someone deeply and to totter along on unsteady legs.

clue.text: The hopelessness Christian found gigantic?

parts.note: surface reading: a believer finding his own hopelessness overwhelming
setter's reading: Christian is the hero of Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress, who is imprisoned by a giant named after hopelessness

explanation.surface: A churchgoer finds his loss of hope enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: Christian is not any believer but the pilgrim in Bunyan's allegory, who is locked in Doubting Castle by Giant Despair.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the plain word for hopelessness, and in Bunyan's book it is the name of a literal giant.

clue.text: Reliance on property administrators

definitions.meaning: first meaning: confidence placed in someone

definitions.note: a body of trustees managing assets for others
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an organisation of trustees holding assets for beneficiaries

explanation.surface: Depending on the people who manage an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Trust means confident dependence, and a trust is also a legal body whose trustees hold and manage assets.

clue.text: One cooking a hot pie in Addis Ababa?

definitions.text: One cooking a hot pie in Addis Ababa?

indicators.note: cooking works ingredients into something new, so the letters that follow are mixed up

parts.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook baking a hot pie in Ethiopia's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: someone in Addis Ababa is quite likely a native of that country.
explanation.definitionFit: Addis Ababa is the capital of Ethiopia, so a person living and cooking there is likely an Ethiopian national.

clue.text: He needs a kid, perhaps, for this game

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A man needs a child to play this game with.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: you do need a child to play it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hide-and-seek is a children's game in which one player searches for the others.

clue.text: Diamonds found in Laodicea

indicators.note: found in says the letters are sitting inside the next word, waiting to be spotted

parts.note: three consecutive letters near the end of the place name

explanation.surface: Jewels unearthed in the ancient city of Laodicea.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is underworld slang for diamonds, from their cold, clear glitter.

clue.text: Popular island peak where chickens may be hatched

parts.note: in means fashionable
Cuba is a Caribbean island
a tor is a rocky hilltop

explanation.surface: A favourite hill on an island where hens raise chicks.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubator is an apparatus that keeps eggs warm so the chicks develop and emerge.

clue.text: Coach rides organized by head of entertainment in York, say

indicators.note: to organise is to put things in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: Coach trips laid on by the head of entertainment for visitors to York.
explanation.walkthrough: York looks like the place the coach rides are in, but it is the definition: it is an example of an archbishop's see.
explanation.definitionFit: York is the seat of an archbishop, so its church district is one example of this kind of diocese.

clue.text: Manipulative type who works his fingers to the bone?

definitions.text: Manipulative type who works his fingers to the bone?

parts.words: Manipulative type who works his fingers to the bone?
parts.note: surface reading: a scheming, hard-grafting person
setter's reading: a therapist who manipulates the skeleton with the hands

explanation.surface: A scheming character who slaves away tirelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: Manipulative sounds like scheming, but it means treating by hand; working fingers to the bone is literal for a practitioner who presses on bones.
explanation.definitionFit: This practitioner treats ailments by manipulating bones and joints with the hands.

clue.text: Accommodating sick aunt, initially, during illness

indicators.note: during means taking place within, so these letters go inside the word for illness

parts.note: a complaint is an ailment

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: first letters of both words

explanation.surface: Being obliging to a poorly aunt when she is ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaisant person is eager to please and willingly goes along with others, which is being accommodating.

clue.text: A gull on the heath, crying feebly

parts.note: a mew is a seagull
ling is heather, the plant of the heath; on places it next in a down clue

explanation.surface: A seagull on the moors, giving a weak cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mewling means whimpering or crying weakly, like a baby or a kitten.

clue.text: A receiver's habitual posture

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a radio or TV apparatus
second meaning: the way one usually holds the body

explanation.surface: How someone receiving something tends to stand.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as is: a receiver is one thing, and so is a habitual posture.
explanation.definitionFit: A television is called a set, and the characteristic carriage of a head or shoulders is also its set.

clue.text: Sigh when a girl tears up the contents

indicators.note: the contents are what is inside, so the reversed word goes within the name

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rips means tears

explanation.surface: A girl sighs as she rips up what is inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspire is a literary word meaning to breathe out, especially in a long sigh.

clue.text: Dismissed without food, becoming weak at the knees?

definitions.note: a cryptic hint: bandy legs are weak at the knees in shape

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the dismissal word goes around the food

parts.note: in cricket a batsman is out bowled when the ball hits the stumps
an egg is an item of food

explanation.surface: Turned away hungry and feeling faint and wobbly.
explanation.walkthrough: Without seems to mean lacking, but here it means outside. Bowled is a way of being out in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Bow-legged people have legs curving outward so the knees stay apart, a playful sense of weak knees.

clue.text: Throw out a former gymnastics student

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
PE is physical education
a learner driver displays an L-plate

explanation.surface: Kicking out an old gymnastics pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel someone is to eject or banish them, especially from a school.

clue.text: Bird seen in river and lake

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, among others in England
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A bird spotted by the water's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel, or ouzel, is an old name for the blackbird and also the water ouzel, or dipper.

clue.text: Old physician finds shelter overlooking church

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side
CH is short for church

explanation.surface: An old doctor takes cover above the church.
explanation.walkthrough: Overlooking positions the shelter above the church in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Leech is an archaic word for a doctor, from the days when bloodsucking worms were used in medicine.

clue.text: One taking off without a shilling as a tourist

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for the coin is taken away

parts.note: someone who takes off clothes
s was the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin

explanation.surface: Someone flying off on holiday with no spending money.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking off suggests flying, but it means undressing. A shilling was a pre-1971 British coin, abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripper is a British word for someone on a short pleasure outing, a day tourist.

clue.text: Ridicule familiar to 16

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to tease someone playfully

definitions.note: a bone, the kind of thing an osteopath works on
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a bone that a bone specialist (the answer to 16 down) knows well

explanation.surface: Mockery that the bone manipulator knows all about.
explanation.definitionFit: To rib is to tease, and a rib is a curved chest bone, standard territory for a bone practitioner.

clue.text: Cagey about endorsement rejected the day before

indicators.note: rejected suggests being sent back, so the word for endorsement is read backwards
about means surrounding, so the evening word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: the eve is the day before a festival
a visa is an endorsement stamped in a passport

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to be pinned down about a permit turned down the previous day.
explanation.definitionFit: A cagey person is guarded and unwilling to give straight answers, the same as an evasive one.

clue.text: Befitting a monarch, to entertain lavishly out East

indicators.note: out means removed, so the compass letter is dropped

parts.note: to regale guests is to feast them
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A royal style of hosting grand dinners in the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal describes what belongs to or suits a king or queen, such as splendid royal bearing.

clue.text: Footballer, say, with novel he's revised for little money

indicators.note: say asks for the sound of the footballer word, spelt differently

parts.note: a back is a defensive footballer

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: She is the novel by Rider Haggard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A footballer whose novel has been edited earns only a pittance.
explanation.walkthrough: With is a plain joining word here; the novel is H. Rider Haggard's She, a stock crossword reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Baksheesh is a small tip or gratuity paid in parts of the Middle East and South Asia.
